divergences: Butterfly schedule: both impls inferred the same Longa–Naehrig CT(forward)/GS(inverse) pair, but the spec only pins 'DIT, merged psi-twist' as a functional result — the actual butterfly schedule is reproduction-chosen.

Output ordering: both produce a bit-reversed intermediate and relabel to 'natural order' functionally, rather than implementing the paper's no-bit-reversal conflict-free datapath — internal order treated as free because only the round-trip result is pinned.

Conflict-free bank-index/offset functions and per-stage crossbar permutation σ_s: both invented their own GF(2) XOR-fold map (admittedly reproduction-chosen); the spec does not transcribe the paper's Sec. III mapping.
Twiddle-ROM addressing f(stage,block) under the rearranged loop: both assumed standard 2^stage+block bit-reversed layout; spec marks it [source-missing].

Radix-4 full transform schedule: neither built an end-to-end radix-4 NTT scheduler — only proved the fused butterfly == DFT-4; the fused two-stage pass + radix-4 conflict-free addressing is not concretely given.
Radix-4 stage cycle accounting is internally inconsistent (impl 2 flags 5*64=320 vs spec's total_bf_cycles_r4=160 / 32 per stage); impl 1 did not resolve it.
Op-count: config_radix_selector says radix-4 BU = 3 mults while the metadata reconciliation says optimized = 2 mults (+8 add/sub vs naive 3+10); both impls flagged it as non-assertable.

structural_findings: The paper's defining feature — the conflict-free interleaved-bank mapping and per-stage crossbar permutation — is replaced by a reproduction-chosen XOR-fold in both impls; the actual routing topology is unverified.

Neither impl builds an end-to-end radix-4 NTT scheduler; the scalable radix-2/4 datapath (the architecture's title claim) is only present as a proven butterfly equivalence, not a working radix-4 transform.
Both rely on a bit-reversed intermediate with functional relabeling, inverting the paper's no-bit-reversal claim at the structural level even though I/O matches.
Radix-4 cycle/op-count accounting in the spec is internally contradictory (3 vs 2 mults; 32 vs 64 cycles/stage), so the impls could not faithfully reproduce the radix-4 schedule even if they tried.

summary: Reproducibility is solid on the arithmetic core — both impls independently converged on identical, fully-specified parameters (N=1024, q=12289, psi=1945, omega=10302, Ninv=12277, Barrett mu/k, 8 BUs, 14-bit) and a verified negacyclic NTT/INTT round-trip — but the spec leaves the paper's signature contributions (the conflict-free bank/crossbar mapping, the rearranged-loop twiddle addressing, and the full radix-4 fusion schedule) untranscribed, with internally contradictory radix-4 op-count/cycle fields, so the two impls diverge into self-invented XOR-fold maps. The biggest fidelity gap mirrors this: the implementations reproduce a generically-correct negacyclic NTT with the right numbers, but NOT the specific CFNTT architecture — conflict-free mapping and no-bit-reversal are unverified/violated structurally, and the radix-2/4 scalability and quantified savings are unverifiable, so they match the system's parameters far better than its defining structure.

guessed: NTT algorithm structure -> CT/DIT forward + GS/DIF inverse, merged-negacyclic (Longa-Naehrig style); spec said 'DIT, merged psi-twist' but not the butterfly schedule
twiddle table contents -> zetas[i]=psi^brv(i), inverse zetas[i]=psi^-brv(i); spec gave only a seed power table + generator g=11
ROM addressing f(stage,block) -> standard CT base 2^s sequential indexing; spec admits the paper's rearranged-loop addressing is not transcribed
output ordering -> forward produces bit-reversed, reconciled to the claimed 'natural order' via the memory map / bit-reversal relabeling (modeled functionally)
inverse normalization -> single multiply by N^-1=12277, no separate psi^-j post-twist pass (merged)

radix-4 FULL transform schedule -> NOT implemented; only the radix-4 butterfly (DFT4 of twiddled inputs) is proven == two radix-2 stages, since the spec calls the full radix-4 schedule 'reconstructed'
bank-conflict argument -> butterfly operands at stride 2^s differ by exactly bit s (no carry), so the GF(2)-linear XOR-fold gives distinct banks; derived from CT group pairing, not stated
per-test-size root -> psi_n = PSI^(1024/n) so each reduced N keeps q=12289 with a primitive 2N-th root
host DMA/PCIe + FIFO interfaces -> not functionally modeled (no datapath/value effect; pure I/O boundary)
radix-4 j-rotator -> j = psi^512 used as the DFT4 fourth root (spec stated this)

Full NTT dataflow -> implemented the standard Longa–Naehrig negacyclic CT(forward)/GS(inverse) butterfly pair with a bit-reversed intermediate ordering; spec claims natural-order / no-bit-reversal conflict-free scheduling, but only the FUNCTIONAL result (round-trip + negacyclic convolution) is pinned, so I match the result and treat the internal order as free

Radix-4 datapath -> verified the radix-4 butterfly UNIT equals a DFT-4 of the twisted inputs (j=psi^512), but did NOT build a full end-to-end radix-4 NTT scheduler (the spec's fused two-stage pass + conflict-free addressing for radix-4 is not concretely given)
Twiddle ROM addressing f(stage,block)=2^stage+block and bit-reversed psi-power layout -> assumed (spec marks it [source-missing])
Host DMA/PCIe framing/handshake -> ignored as non-functional (spec itself calls it a reproduction-only abstraction)
Pipeline latency 9 cycles (mult3+addsub1+Barrett4+reg1) -> timing only, not modeled in the functional/value verification
FSM transition semantics -> taken verbatim from schedule_controller.transitions; only checked as a reachability graph, not as cycle-accurate control
j-rotator convention (y1/y3 sign) -> took the spec's exact y0..y3 equations, which correspond to a forward DFT-4 with root j; an inverse/conjugate convention would swap y1<->y3
